Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

so … that conjunction

result

also so that (result), such … that, so much … that, so … as to, with the result that

classical

Sen. Ep. 57.1: tantum lutī tōtā viā fuit ut possim vidērī nihilōminus nāvigāsse
Liv. 21.56.7: ita torpentēs gelū in castra rediēre ut vix laetitiam victōriae sentīrent

ut (+ subjunctive), after ita, sīc, tam, adeō, tantus, tālis

conjunction, with the subjunctive; negative ut nōn

The main clause usually has the pointer word (ita, sīc, tam, adeō, tantus, tālis). Unlike purpose, the negative is ut nōn, and the tense may break the sequence to state a plain past fact (ut … prōdiderit).

Other words

  • quīn (+ subjunctive) — that … not (after a negative)

    conjunction, with the subjunctive, after a negative main clause · also used · classical · Ter. Haut. 675: Nihil tam difficile est quīn quaerendō investīgārī possiet.

    “Nothing is so hard that it cannot …”: quīn = ut nōn after a negative.

Examples

  • tantum lutī tōtā viā fuit ut possim vidērī nihilōminus nāvigāsse

    there was so much mud the whole way that I might as well have gone by seaSen. Ep. 57.1

  • nōs enim ita philologī sumus ut vel cum fabrīs habitāre possīmus

    for we are such bookworms that we could even live with the builders inCic. Q. fr. 2.8.3

  • ita torpentēs gelū in castra rediēre ut vix laetitiam victōriae sentīrent

    they came back to camp so numb with cold that they could hardly feel the joy of victoryLiv. 21.56.7

  • nōn tamen adeō virtūtum sterile saeculum ut nōn et bona exempla prōdiderit

    yet the age was not so barren of virtue that it produced no good examplesTac. Hist. 1.3

  • Nihil tam difficile est quīn quaerendō investīgārī possiet.

    Nothing is so hard that it can’t be found out by searching.Ter. Haut. 675

See also so that, so big!, therefore.
